// shapes.ts.txt — SCANNED, NEVER RUN. The grammar allows callee shapes that a
// runnable .mjs cannot spell (TS non-null) or that only appear in positions
// the executable fixture has no use for. They are here so the CLASSIFIER is
// measured against the grammar, while the ORACLE is measured against what
// runs. The two denominators are different and saying so is the point.
//
// THE `.txt` TAIL IS LOAD-BEARING. tsconfig's include covers `test/**/*.ts`,
// so a fixture named `shapes.ts` is COMPILED as part of the project — and a
// fixture whose whole job is to hold odd or deliberately degenerate shapes
// cannot also satisfy tsc. The first version of this file was bent to please
// the compiler (`(0, curried)` grew a side effect to dodge TS2695), which
// silently changed the construct under study. The name keeps `.ts` so the
// reader and the scanner still know what language it is.
declare const maybe: ((n: number) => number) | null;
declare const bag: Record<string, (n: number) => number>;
declare const key: string;

export function tsShapes(n: number): number {
  return maybe!(n) + bag[key](n) + bag['fixed'](n);
}

// A computed callee whose key is a template with no expressions. The value is
// fixed at parse time, and the scanner's four-relation contract cannot carry
// it: TemplateElement.value is `{raw, cooked}`, a nested OBJECT, and only
// scalar own properties become ast_attr facts. So this site is knowable and
// not derivable, which is `not_yet` and emphatically NOT runtime_dependent.
export function tmplKey(n: number): number { return bag[`fixed`](n); }

class Base { m(): number { return 1; } }
export class Sub extends Base {
  constructor() { super(); }
  m(): number { return super.m(); }
}

// TWO SITES ADDED AS A MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-04. The grammar allows a member on
// a fresh instance and a member on an inline object literal; the corpus did
// not contain either, so whether the rules already cover them was a GUESS. A
// site turns the guess into a row. Neither needs a rule if `new C()` reaches
// the class and an object literal is its own value — and if it does need one,
// that is worth knowing before the cell is filled from an argument.
export function onNew(n: number): number { return new Base().m() + n; }
export function onLit(n: number): number { return ({ a(m: number) { return m; } }).a(n); }

function curried(n: number) { return (m: number) => m + n; }
export function chained(n: number): number { return curried(n)(n); }
export function seq(n: number): number { return (0, curried)(n)(n); }
export function cond(n: number, f: (x: number) => number, g: (x: number) => number) {
  return (n > 0 ? f : g)(n);
}
// TWO MORE MEASUREMENT SITES, 2026-09-04, and for the same reason as the last
// pair: `maybe!()` and `(c ? f : g)()` refused, and the refusal was about the
// CORPUS — `maybe` is an ambient declaration with no value, and nobody calls
// `cond`, so its parameters carry nothing. Give each a callee the value layer
// can actually reach and the question becomes about the model instead.
const notNull = curried;
export function useNonNull(n: number): number { return notNull!(n)(n); }
export function useCond(n: number): number { return cond(n, curried(1), curried(2)); }

// a TS cast in the callee position. `s_parenthesized` gets no site on purpose:
// measured 2026-09-04, babel does not emit ParenthesizedExpression under this
// parser configuration at all — `(f)(1)` is a plain identifier callee — so no
// corpus can produce that shape and it is waived rather than left `absent`.
export function useAs(n: number): number {
  return (curried as (m: number) => (k: number) => number)(n)(n);
}

// FOUR MORE OBJECT POSITIONS, and these are here rather than in alpha.mjs for
// a reason that is about the ORACLE. `(x as T).m()` and `x!.m()` cannot be
// spelt in a runnable .mjs at all. `(await p).m()` and `` `s`.m() `` CAN be,
// and they must not be: neither resolves today — the first waits on the
// control-form item and the second answers through the String prototype, which
// is the standard library — so a runnable site would show up as an edge the
// runtime takes and the model misses, which is UNSOUND. A shape whose residue
// is known and owned belongs in the corpus the oracle does not run.
// EVERY RECEIVER BELOW IS A REAL VALUE, and that is the whole care taken here.
// The first draft wrote `declare const held: Holder | null` and asked whether
// `held!.pick()` resolves — it does not, and the refusal would have been about
// an ambient declaration carrying no value rather than about the model. The
// same trap caught the `(cast as T)` probe an hour earlier and `maybe!()` in
// this very file a day earlier. A site measures the model only when everything
// except the construct under study already works.
const holder = { pick(n: number): number { return n; } };
type Holder = typeof holder;
async function mkHolder(): Promise<Holder> { return holder; }

export function onCast(n: number): number { return (holder as Holder).pick(n); }
export function onNonNull(n: number): number { return holder!.pick(n); }
// `mkHolder()` alone DOES reach `holder` through the return rule, so the only
// thing standing between this site and an edge is the `await` wrapper — which
// is `w_df_control_forms`, and this site is what will show it landing.
export async function onAwait(n: number): Promise<number> {
  return (await mkHolder()).pick(n);
}
// The receiver here is a String, not a value in this program: `concat` answers
// through the built-in prototype. Its residue is the standard library.
export function onTemplate(n: number): string { return `k${n}`.concat('!'); }

export async function dyn(p: string) { return import(p); }
